records.title: P001 — Ground stakeholder and mission intent in authoritative, current evidence

scientific_record.Property name: Ground stakeholder and mission intent in authoritative, current evidence
scientific_record.Historical origin: Hall's problem-definition and goal-setting tradition; NASA stakeholder-expectations practice; requirements-engineering work on environment and agreement.
scientific_record.Original form: Identify customer objectives and translate them into system goals before detailed design.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: Component teams can optimise a technically impressive solution that does not solve the governing mission or current stakeholder problem.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: Solution success is asserted against an unauthorised, stale or internally invented notion of value.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Record the intended outcomes, sources, decision authority, conflicts, use context, assumptions and current validation evidence; make downstream decisions point back to that governed intent.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: Multiple stakeholders; costly or irreversible design; regulated/contractual commitments; uncertain mission; long lifecycle; changed operating context.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: For a small reversible task with one empowered user and immediate feedback, a dated goal statement plus direct confirmation is enough.
scientific_record.Dependencies or preconditions: Access to representative stakeholders or mission evidence; explicit system boundary and intended lifecycle; a means to resolve or preserve disagreement.
scientific_record.Stakeholder or mission preconditions: The governing need, stakeholder classes, intended use and current context must be identifiable; latent/absent stakeholders are a declared limitation.
scientific_record.Authority preconditions: A named person, body, law, contract or mission authority must be able to legitimise or change the governing intent; facilitation is not authority.
scientific_record.Configuration or identity preconditions: The intent record, source and applicable system/configuration/time horizon must be versioned.
scientific_record.Interface or integration preconditions: External actors, environments and ecosystem dependencies that affect intent must be within scope.
scientific_record.Evidence or vv preconditions: Validation evidence must be capable of challenging the stated need and intended-use model.
scientific_record.Expected payoff asserted at this source: Conditional intended benefit: reduce the relevant likelihood, detection delay or consequence of Solution success is asserted against an unauthorised, stale or internally invented notion of value. This is a mechanism-based hypothesis, not a measured universal causal effect. Compare information, coordination and avoided-loss benefits with total cost for the named decision consumer.
scientific_record.Decision or consumer: Mission owner, product owner, architecture authority, requirements authority and validation authority.
scientific_record.Known failure modes: Solution-biased framing; token stakeholder participation; stale authority; proxy outcomes; hidden conflicts; retrospective rationalisation.
scientific_record.Important criticisms: Stakeholder workshops and CONOPS documents can create consensus theatre; stated requests may reflect politics, solution bias or absent users.
scientific_record.How the property evolved: Original form: Identify customer objectives and translate them into system goals before detailed design. Evolved under criticism into: A living intent model whose authority, recency, conflicts, measures and affected decisions are explicit; revalidate after material change.
scientific_record.Evolved form in this source: A living intent model whose authority, recency, conflicts, measures and affected decisions are explicit; revalidate after material change.
scientific_record.Ceremony vs property: CONOPS, mission statements, stakeholder registers and workshops are optional carriers. The property is current, authoritative intent that governs and can be challenged.
scientific_record.Empirical or domain evidence: NASA operational guidance is strong; broad comparative outcome evidence is mostly case/survey rather than experimental.
scientific_record.Contrary evidence: No representation can prove latent future needs are complete; authority may be contested.
scientific_record.Open questions: How should latent, future and non-participating stakeholders be weighted without inventing authority?

scientific_record.Property name: Separate validated need and problem from proposed solution
scientific_record.Historical origin: Systems-analysis problem-of-choice work; Hall; requirements-engineering environment/machine distinctions.
scientific_record.Original form: Define the problem, objectives and alternatives before selecting a system concept.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: An early preferred technology is smuggled into the requirement, suppressing cheaper or more effective alternatives.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: A design is verified perfectly against a requirement that merely restates the preselected solution.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Express outcomes, constraints and environmental conditions separately from candidate means; label mandated design constraints and their authority.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: Early concept selection; competing technologies; high switching cost; ambiguous requests; procurement language that embeds a product.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: Where the mandated implementation is genuinely fixed by law, interoperability or owner authority, record that constraint and skip artificial alternative generation.
scientific_record.Dependencies or preconditions: Access to representative stakeholders or mission evidence; explicit system boundary and intended lifecycle; a means to resolve or preserve disagreement.
scientific_record.Stakeholder or mission preconditions: The governing need, stakeholder classes, intended use and current context must be identifiable; latent/absent stakeholders are a declared limitation.

scientific_record.Configuration or identity preconditions: The intent record, source and applicable system/configuration/time horizon must be versioned.
scientific_record.Interface or integration preconditions: External actors, environments and ecosystem dependencies that affect intent must be within scope.
scientific_record.Evidence or vv preconditions: Validation evidence must be capable of challenging the stated need and intended-use model.
scientific_record.Expected payoff asserted at this source: Conditional intended benefit: reduce the relevant likelihood, detection delay or consequence of A design is verified perfectly against a requirement that merely restates the preselected solution. This is a mechanism-based hypothesis, not a measured universal causal effect. Compare information, coordination and avoided-loss benefits with total cost for the named decision consumer.
scientific_record.Decision or consumer: Mission owner, product owner, architecture authority, requirements authority and validation authority.
scientific_record.Known failure modes: Solution-biased framing; token stakeholder participation; stale authority; proxy outcomes; hidden conflicts; retrospective rationalisation.
scientific_record.Important criticisms: The distinction is not absolute: some needs are only discoverable through prototypes, and architecture can reshape feasible goals.
scientific_record.How the property evolved: Original form: Define the problem, objectives and alternatives before selecting a system concept. Evolved under criticism into: Maintain an explicit need–solution boundary, with exceptions justified by named authority and revisited when constraints change.

scientific_record.Property name: Govern outcome, mission and effectiveness measures
scientific_record.Historical origin: Systems analysis and early SE effectiveness evaluation; NASA measures of effectiveness and mission engineering.
scientific_record.Original form: Define quantitative objectives and effectiveness criteria for comparing candidate systems.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: Teams optimise easy technical proxies that are disconnected from mission outcomes or whose thresholds no longer reflect stakeholder value.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: A dashboard stays green while the delivered capability remains unusable or strategically irrelevant.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Tie each outcome measure to a named stakeholder/mission claim, decision, threshold/objective, measurement context, uncertainty and refresh condition.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: Architecture trades; mission/capability portfolios; performance competition; changing operational priorities.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: Where direct user feedback immediately settles value, use it instead of constructing a metric hierarchy.
scientific_record.Dependencies or preconditions: Access to representative stakeholders or mission evidence; explicit system boundary and intended lifecycle; a means to resolve or preserve disagreement.

scientific_record.Property name: Preserve options, reversibility and decision-reopening triggers
scientific_record.Historical origin: Set-based design and evolutionary/iterative engineering.
scientific_record.Original form: Delay selection while maturing alternatives and revisit decisions when evidence changes.

scientific_record.Mechanism: Traverse current semantic dependencies; challenge assumptions and non-local interactions; classify certain, possible and unknown impacts; assign rework/revalidation owners.

scientific_record.Evidence or vv preconditions: Evidence must cite configuration and be invalidated or justified after change.

This is a mechanism-based hypothesis, not a measured universal causal effect. Compare information, coordination and avoided-loss benefits with total cost for the named decision consumer.

records.title: P031 — Plan integration strategy, sequence and readiness

scientific_record.Property name: Plan integration strategy, sequence and readiness
scientific_record.Historical origin: Aerospace/space programme integration and NASA lifecycle practice.
scientific_record.Original form: Create an assembly, integration and test plan for bottom-up system realisation.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: Products arrive in an order or maturity state that blocks useful integration, hides high-risk interfaces or consumes scarce facilities inefficiently.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: The first system-level composition occurs after architecture and supplier choices are hard to change.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Order integration by risk, dependency and learning value; define entry evidence, facilities, configurations, owners, fallback paths and anomaly flow.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: Multiple components/suppliers; scarce testbeds; hardware/software coupling; high integration risk.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: Two-component low-risk work may integrate directly under a short checklist.
scientific_record.Dependencies or preconditions: Defined interfaces/configurations, integration authority, suitable environments, entry evidence, anomaly process and feasible sequencing.
scientific_record.Stakeholder or mission preconditions: Integration must exercise the mission/use interactions that matter, not only convenient assembly paths.
scientific_record.Authority preconditions: Someone must control integration configuration, sequence, facilities, discrepancy disposition and stop/go decisions.
scientific_record.Configuration or identity preconditions: Every integration result must identify products, software/data, environment, tools and configuration.
scientific_record.Interface or integration preconditions: Risky semantic, timing, physical, organisational and state interfaces are first-class targets.
scientific_record.Evidence or vv preconditions: Integration evidence is not automatically verification or validation; claims, coverage and limitations must be stated.
scientific_record.Expected payoff asserted at this source: Conditional intended benefit: reduce the relevant likelihood, detection delay or consequence of The first system-level composition occurs after architecture and supplier choices are hard to change. This is a mechanism-based hypothesis, not a measured universal causal effect. Compare information, coordination and avoided-loss benefits with total cost for the named decision consumer.
scientific_record.Decision or consumer: Integration lead, architecture/interface owners, V&V authorities, release authority and operators.
scientific_record.Known failure modes: Late big-bang composition; low-fidelity surrogate overclaim; schedule-driven readiness waivers; anomaly closure theatre; component-pass/system-fail.
scientific_record.Important criticisms: Detailed plans become obsolete; readiness criteria can be gamed; schedule pressure encourages paper waivers.
scientific_record.How the property evolved: Original form: Create an assembly, integration and test plan for bottom-up system realisation. Evolved under criticism into: A living risk/learning strategy that determines what is combined next and why, rather than a date-driven final-assembly schedule.
scientific_record.Evolved form in this source: A living risk/learning strategy that determines what is combined next and why, rather than a date-driven final-assembly schedule.
scientific_record.Ceremony vs property: Integration plans and readiness reviews are optional carriers. The property is early enough, risk-ranked composition evidence.
scientific_record.Empirical or domain evidence: Strong programme guidance and case evidence; comparative sequence studies are scarce.
scientific_record.Contrary evidence: Integration sequence optimisation is often heuristic and resource-constrained.
scientific_record.Open questions: How should learning value, failure containment and facility scarcity be traded in sequence design?

scientific_record.Original form: Analyse system behaviour by composing subsystem functions.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: Interactions, feedback, adaptation and organisational response create behaviours not predictable from isolated component properties.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: All allocated requirements pass yet mission behaviour is unstable, unsafe or ineffective.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Identify feedback, modes, shared resources, nonlinearities, adaptation and plausible interaction paths; use simulation, scenario exploration, integration and operational monitoring.

records.title: P044 — Tailor systems-engineering depth to consequence, complexity, uncertainty and reversibility

scientific_record.Property name: Tailor systems-engineering depth to consequence, complexity, uncertainty and reversibility
scientific_record.Historical origin: Lifecycle standards, defence pathway tailoring, agile SE and very-small-entity profiles.
scientific_record.Original form: Tailor standard processes and artefacts to project size and lifecycle.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: Full ceremony is imposed on cheap reversible work, or critical cross-boundary work is declared 'agile' and left without adequate evidence.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: Engineering effort is either wasted or underpowered relative to actual risk.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Scale representation, authority, independence, traceability, modelling, review and V&V to consequence, coupling, novelty, distribution, irreversibility and evidence fragility; retain a documented cheap path.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: Every project; especially heterogeneous portfolios and mixed hardware/software.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: Local reversible work should use direct evidence, short records and immediate feedback unless a trigger appears.
scientific_record.Dependencies or preconditions: A transparent trigger model, authority to tailor, minimum non-waivable obligations and feedback on actual engineering outcomes.
scientific_record.Stakeholder or mission preconditions: Consequence and value are judged against current stakeholder/mission commitments.
scientific_record.Authority preconditions: Tailoring decisions require named authority and cannot be self-exemption by the work producer alone where consequence is high.
scientific_record.Configuration or identity preconditions: Applicable lifecycle, product, change and evidence scope must be identified.
scientific_record.Interface or integration preconditions: Coupling, organisational distribution and interface complexity are core escalation triggers.
scientific_record.Evidence or vv preconditions: Evidence fragility, consequence and reversibility determine review/V&V depth.
scientific_record.Expected payoff asserted at this source: Conditional intended benefit: reduce the relevant likelihood, detection delay or consequence of Engineering effort is either wasted or underpowered relative to actual risk. This is a mechanism-based hypothesis, not a measured universal causal effect. Compare information, coordination and avoided-loss benefits with total cost for the named decision consumer.
scientific_record.Decision or consumer: Technical authority, project/product leadership, assurance authority and teams executing the cheap path.
scientific_record.Known failure modes: Blanket process; arbitrary waivers; size-only scaling; process accretion; inherited controls with no consumer; under-assurance under 'agile' labels.
scientific_record.Important criticisms: Tailoring can become arbitrary omission or negotiation by the most powerful team; standards offer little empirical calibration.
scientific_record.How the property evolved: Original form: Tailor standard processes and artefacts to project size and lifecycle. Evolved under criticism into: A trigger-based assurance architecture with explicit escalation and de-escalation, not project-size folklore or blanket waivers.
scientific_record.Evolved form in this source: A trigger-based assurance architecture with explicit escalation and de-escalation, not project-size folklore or blanket waivers.
scientific_record.Ceremony vs property: Tailoring matrices and plans are optional. The property is explicit activation/deactivation of engineering machinery by evidence-bearing triggers.
scientific_record.Empirical or domain evidence: Very strong standards/guidance support; numerical ROI and threshold evidence is mixed/weak.
scientific_record.Contrary evidence: Evidence does not yield universal trigger thresholds or effort percentages.
scientific_record.Open questions: How can proportionality be measured and audited without recreating process bureaucracy?

records.title: P045 — Engineer distributed authority and federated governance in systems of systems

scientific_record.Property name: Engineer distributed authority and federated governance in systems of systems
scientific_record.Historical origin: Maier's SoS definition, DoD SoS guidance and ISO 21839.
scientific_record.Original form: Coordinate constituent-system managers under a SoS capability office.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: A central architecture assumes authority it does not possess; constituents optimise local missions and schedules.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: Global capability plans fail because dependencies cannot be compelled or synchronised.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Map real decision rights, incentives, commitments, escalation, voluntary standards and fallback options; design governance around managerial and operational independence.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: Constituent systems have independent ownership, resources, goals and lifecycle.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: Ordinary multi-team systems under one enforceable authority should use normal interface/configuration governance instead.
scientific_record.Dependencies or preconditions: Demonstrated operational and managerial independence, mission-level dependence, constituent identities, real authority map and communication mechanisms.
scientific_record.Stakeholder or mission preconditions: Global mission legitimacy and each constituent's local stakeholders/goals must both be represented.
scientific_record.Authority preconditions: Central authority limits, constituent sovereignty, incentives, agreements and escalation must be explicit.
scientific_record.Configuration or identity preconditions: Constituent versions, membership, compatibility and mission configurations change asynchronously and must be tracked.
scientific_record.Interface or integration preconditions: Interoperability spans technical, semantic, organisational and policy interfaces.
scientific_record.Evidence or vv preconditions: Mission-thread and runtime/operational evidence must supplement constituent verification.
scientific_record.Expected payoff asserted at this source: Conditional intended benefit: reduce the relevant likelihood, detection delay or consequence of Global capability plans fail because dependencies cannot be compelled or synchronised. This is a mechanism-based hypothesis, not a measured universal causal effect. Compare information, coordination and avoided-loss benefits with total cost for the named decision consumer.
scientific_record.Decision or consumer: Mission/capability owner, constituent owners, interoperability/integration authorities and operators.
scientific_record.Known failure modes: Fictional central control; voluntary compliance without incentive; stale global architecture; local optimisation; asynchronous drift; untestable dynamic compositions.
scientific_record.Important criticisms: Governance frameworks often lack enforceable authority and can become coordination forums without consequence.
scientific_record.How the property evolved: Original form: Coordinate constituent-system managers under a SoS capability office. Evolved under criticism into: Federated governance that states where authority ends and uses incentives/contracts/evidence rather than fictional central control.
scientific_record.Evolved form in this source: Federated governance that states where authority ends and uses incentives/contracts/evidence rather than fictional central control.
scientific_record.Ceremony vs property: SoS boards and architecture frameworks are optional. The property is federated coordination under real independence and evolving composition.
scientific_record.Empirical or domain evidence: Strong definitional/guidance support; outcome evidence is largely case-based.
scientific_record.Contrary evidence: No general mechanism resolves persistent conflict among sovereign constituents.
scientific_record.Open questions: What minimum commitments make global mission claims legitimate in a voluntary SoS?

scientific_record.Property name: Use model-centred representation only when it carries engineering decisions
scientific_record.Historical origin: Wymore's formal MBSE lineage, NASA modelling and modern MBSE.
scientific_record.Original form: Replace document-centric SE with a coherent system model.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: A large model is built because MBSE is mandated but does not improve analysis, coordination, change or V&V.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: Model maintenance adds cost while real decisions continue in slides, spreadsheets and tacit knowledge.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Define model questions, users, decisions and generated evidence before modelling; choose scope/language/fidelity accordingly; measure use and retire unused views.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: High relationship density; repeated analysis; multiple viewpoints; automation/interchange opportunity; long lifecycle.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: For a simple project, structured text, tables, executable tests or sketches may be superior.
scientific_record.Dependencies or preconditions: Named model questions/consumers, governance, skilled users, versioning, tool/data access, validation and sustainable maintenance economics.

scientific_record.Property name: Federate models semantically and preserve representation portability
scientific_record.Historical origin: Semantic interoperability, model federation and SysML/API standardisation.
scientific_record.Original form: Exchange models among tools through common formats and maintain a model repository.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: Tools exchange files or identifiers while meanings, constraints, behaviour and provenance are lost or transformed silently.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: A digital thread presents connected artefacts that are not semantically equivalent.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Define canonical semantics/ontologies where justified; test transformations; record losses; expose inconsistency; preserve export/API access and tool-exit paths.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: Multiple engineering disciplines/tools/suppliers; long-lived data; regulated handover; acquisition lock-in risk.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: One-team/one-tool short-lived work can use a stable open export and documented schema.

scientific_record.Historical origin: Configuration/change control, contingency planning and continuous delivery translation.
scientific_record.Original form: Provide backout plans and contingency actions for changes and releases.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: A technically approved change cannot be reversed or isolated after integration/operation reveals unexpected effects.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: The system remains in a degraded or unsafe configuration while diagnosis continues.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Classify reversibility, preserve recoverable state/configurations, define stop/rollback criteria, practise recovery where consequential, and bound irreversible transitions.

scientific_record.Evidence or vv preconditions: Evidence must cite configuration and be invalidated or justified after change.

This is a mechanism-based hypothesis, not a measured universal causal effect. Compare information, coordination and avoided-loss benefits with total cost for the named decision consumer.

scientific_record.Important criticisms: Rollback can be impossible for physical changes, database evolution, learned/adaptive state or external ecosystem effects; dual paths add complexity.

scientific_record.Property name: Include enabling systems and lifecycle stakeholders in system definition
scientific_record.Historical origin: Lifecycle SE and concurrent engineering.
scientific_record.Original form: Plan manufacturing, test, deployment, operation, maintenance, support and disposal alongside the end product.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: The delivered product works only with unavailable test equipment, untrained operators, fragile logistics or unplanned disposal/support.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: Local product optimisation shifts cost and failure into later lifecycle stages or enabling systems.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Model critical enabling systems, stakeholders, interfaces, resources and constraints early enough to influence architecture and evidence.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: Long-lived physical systems; specialised operations; maintainability/logistics; certification; hazardous disposal.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: For short-lived software/services using standard infrastructure, capture only enabling dependencies that can alter feasibility or operation.
scientific_record.Dependencies or preconditions: Defined lifecycle/system boundary, representative lifecycle stakeholders, dependency/economic rationale and configuration/feedback mechanisms.
scientific_record.Stakeholder or mission preconditions: Operators, maintainers, manufacturers, support, disposal, regulators and portfolio/mission actors are included only where materially affected.
scientific_record.Authority preconditions: Authority across lifecycle organisations and product-family/mission boundaries must be explicit.
scientific_record.Configuration or identity preconditions: Product variants, enabling systems, operational populations and lifecycle states must be identifiable.
scientific_record.Interface or integration preconditions: Enabling-system, human, platform and mission dependencies are treated as interfaces/compositions.
scientific_record.Evidence or vv preconditions: Operational, maintainability, variability and mission evidence must match the claimed lifecycle scope.
scientific_record.Expected payoff asserted at this source: Conditional intended benefit: reduce the relevant likelihood, detection delay or consequence of Local product optimisation shifts cost and failure into later lifecycle stages or enabling systems. This is a mechanism-based hypothesis, not a measured universal causal effect. Compare information, coordination and avoided-loss benefits with total cost for the named decision consumer.
scientific_record.Decision or consumer: Product/mission owner, architect, operations/support, platform governance and lifecycle authorities.
scientific_record.Known failure modes: Unbounded scope; speculative future modelling; commonality overreach; lifecycle stakeholder tokenism; duplication with programme/logistics functions.
scientific_record.Important criticisms: Lifecycle scope can expand without bound; future support/disposal assumptions are uncertain.
scientific_record.How the property evolved: Original form: Plan manufacturing, test, deployment, operation, maintenance, support and disposal alongside the end product. Evolved under criticism into: Selective whole-lifecycle inclusion driven by consequence and dependency, not exhaustive lifecycle documentation.
scientific_record.Evolved form in this source: Selective whole-lifecycle inclusion driven by consequence and dependency, not exhaustive lifecycle documentation.

scientific_record.Contrary evidence: Benefits are difficult to isolate from programme management and logistics practices.

records.title: P054 — Allocate functions and authority across hardware, software, humans and organisations

scientific_record.Property name: Allocate functions and authority across hardware, software, humans and organisations
scientific_record.Historical origin: Human-systems integration and systems architecting.
scientific_record.Original form: Assign system functions to people, hardware and software.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: Automation or organisational design allocates tasks without considering human capability, workload, authority, observability, training or recovery.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: The technical system passes but operators cannot control, understand, maintain or safely recover it.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Treat allocation as an architecture decision with operating context, authority, handoff/interface, performance assumptions and validation with representative users.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: Human-in/on-the-loop systems; autonomy; complex maintenance; high workload; organisational handoffs.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: Simple tools with direct user control may validate allocation through ordinary use tests.
scientific_record.Dependencies or preconditions: Defined lifecycle/system boundary, representative lifecycle stakeholders, dependency/economic rationale and configuration/feedback mechanisms.

This is a mechanism-based hypothesis, not a measured universal causal effect. Compare information, coordination and avoided-loss benefits with total cost for the named decision consumer.

scientific_record.Known failure modes: Unbounded scope; speculative future modelling; commonality overreach; lifecycle stakeholder tokenism; duplication with programme/logistics functions.
scientific_record.Important criticisms: This property shares ancestry with human factors; detailed cognitive-fit methods lie outside this lane.

scientific_record.Historical origin: Product-line engineering and platform/commonality traditions.

scientific_record.Known failure modes: Unbounded scope; speculative future modelling; commonality overreach; lifecycle stakeholder tokenism; duplication with programme/logistics functions.

records.title: P057 — Use AI-assisted requirements, architecture and modelling under human, provenance and validation controls

scientific_record.Property name: Use AI-assisted requirements, architecture and modelling under human, provenance and validation controls
scientific_record.Historical origin: Recent AI-for-RE, AI-for-architecture and AI-for-MBSE research; no settled direct historical lineage.
scientific_record.Original form: Generate, classify, link or analyse engineering artefacts with large language models and other AI.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: Plausible outputs, trace links or models are accepted without source authority, reproducibility, semantic validation or configuration control.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: Automation scales hallucination, bias and false coherence into an authoritative engineering baseline.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Constrain use cases; preserve prompts/models/data/tool versions and sources; require domain review, deterministic checks and independent evidence for consequential claims; monitor error and drift.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: High-volume drafting/search; candidate generation; trace recovery; model queries; bounded low-consequence assistance.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: Do not use AI where a deterministic parser/check/query is cheaper and more reliable, or where outputs cannot be adequately validated.
scientific_record.Dependencies or preconditions: Named model questions/consumers, governance, skilled users, versioning, tool/data access, validation and sustainable maintenance economics.
scientific_record.Stakeholder or mission preconditions: Models must represent authorised needs/use and disclose omitted stakeholders/context.
scientific_record.Authority preconditions: Authority is claim-specific; tool/repository ownership does not grant truth authority.
scientific_record.Configuration or identity preconditions: Model, metamodel, tool, data, transformation, implementation and physical referent versions must be related.
scientific_record.Interface or integration preconditions: Semantic interoperability, transformation loss, APIs and supplier/tool boundaries must be tested.
scientific_record.Evidence or vv preconditions: Intended use, verification, validation, uncertainty, provenance, currentness and permissible inference are mandatory for consequential use.
scientific_record.Expected payoff asserted at this source: Conditional intended benefit: reduce the relevant likelihood, detection delay or consequence of Automation scales hallucination, bias and false coherence into an authoritative engineering baseline. This is a mechanism-based hypothesis, not a measured universal causal effect. Compare information, coordination and avoided-loss benefits with total cost for the named decision consumer.
scientific_record.Decision or consumer: Engineers/analysts making decisions, integrators, V&V authorities, operators and lifecycle data users.
scientific_record.Known failure modes: Model volume; staleness; tool lock-in; inconsistent repositories; semantic loss; perceived-benefit bias; automated false coherence; inaccessible expertise.
scientific_record.Important criticisms: Evidence is predominantly early-stage, laboratory and rapidly obsolete; reproducibility, interpretability, hallucination and governance are unresolved.
scientific_record.How the property evolved: Original form: Generate, classify, link or analyse engineering artefacts with large language models and other AI. Evolved under criticism into: AI as a fallible hypothesis and retrieval/translation aid inside governed SE, never an autonomous authority for need, architecture or assurance.

scientific_record.Original form: Store and control technical data, models and records throughout the lifecycle.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: Critical rationale and evidence are inaccessible, duplicated, proprietary, unsearchable or detached from current authority.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: Decisions are repeated, suppliers cannot integrate, maintainers cannot diagnose and reviewers rely on presentation summaries.
scientific_record.Mechanism: Identify authoritative records by claim; preserve provenance, access, portability, retention, version and consumer; distinguish governing, working and historical information.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: Long lifecycle; supplier turnover; regulated evidence; multi-tool environment; sustainment.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: For small work, a well-structured repository with immutable history and clear current pointers may be enough.
scientific_record.Dependencies or preconditions: Governed items, stable identifiers, change authority, status accounting and access to actual product/model/test/environment state.
scientific_record.Stakeholder or mission preconditions: Configuration must be tied to the authorised capability, commitments and operational population.
scientific_record.Authority preconditions: Authority to baseline, change, waive, release, roll back and supersede must be explicit and consequence-tiered.
scientific_record.Configuration or identity preconditions: This family centrally requires exact item/composition/version/environment/evidence identity.
scientific_record.Interface or integration preconditions: Interface and supplier configuration dependencies must be included in impact and release decisions.
scientific_record.Evidence or vv preconditions: Evidence must cite configuration and be invalidated or justified after change.
scientific_record.Expected payoff asserted at this source: Conditional intended benefit: reduce the relevant likelihood, detection delay or consequence of Decisions are repeated, suppliers cannot integrate, maintainers cannot diagnose and reviewers rely on presentation summaries. This is a mechanism-based hypothesis, not a measured universal causal effect. Compare information, coordination and avoided-loss benefits with total cost for the named decision consumer.
scientific_record.Decision or consumer: Builder, integrator, release/change authority, verifier, operator, maintainer, supplier and auditor.
scientific_record.Known failure modes: Frozen-baseline bureaucracy; snapshot proliferation; approved-but-unimplemented changes; hidden environment drift; incomplete impact maps; evidence over/under-invalidation.
scientific_record.Important criticisms: Central repositories create lock-in and stale duplication; access control can block the very cross-boundary use intended.
scientific_record.How the property evolved: Original form: Store and control technical data, models and records throughout the lifecycle. Evolved under criticism into: Technical knowledge continuity as governed access and identity, not accumulation or one-tool centralisation.
scientific_record.Evolved form in this source: Technical knowledge continuity as governed access and identity, not accumulation or one-tool centralisation.
scientific_record.Ceremony vs property: CCBs, forms and baseline reviews are optional. The property is truthful identity, authority, implementation status and evidence continuity.
scientific_record.Empirical or domain evidence: Strong guidance and case rationale; DE measurement evidence remains immature.
scientific_record.Contrary evidence: Empirical benefit and optimal data granularity remain undermeasured.
scientific_record.Open questions: How should proprietary rights, security and lifecycle accessibility be balanced?

Current assessment.Selected proposition: Make engineering data accessible and intelligible to authorized decision consumers at the time and granularity needed.

records.title: P061 — Fixed one-pass V-model or waterfall lifecycle as a universal SE property

scientific_record.Property name: Fixed one-pass V-model or waterfall lifecycle as a universal SE property
scientific_record.Historical origin: Textbook simplification and conflation of multiple V/Vee lineages.
scientific_record.Original form: Complete decomposition/specification once, then implement, integrate and validate once in a fixed sequence.
scientific_record.Problem it addressed: Feedback and requirement change are delayed by process doctrine.
scientific_record.Failure mode it tries to prevent: The lifecycle representation is mistaken for the engineering mechanism.
scientific_record.Mechanism: No retained universal mechanism; preserve only recursive decomposition/composition relationships, early V&V planning and evidence feedback.
scientific_record.Trigger or context: No general trigger. A contract or physical programme may use staged transitions, but that is a context-specific lifecycle choice.
scientific_record.Non trigger or cheap path: Select lifecycle/cadence from risk, reversibility, learning and physical constraints.
scientific_record.Dependencies or preconditions: Not applicable as a retained general property; evaluate the stronger surviving mechanism instead.
scientific_record.Stakeholder or mission preconditions: No artefact or process count can substitute for authoritative stakeholder/mission grounding.
scientific_record.Authority preconditions: Approval does not manufacture technical truth.
scientific_record.Configuration or identity preconditions: Ceremonial artefacts often obscure rather than establish current identity.
scientific_record.Interface or integration preconditions: Formal presence does not establish semantic or behavioural compatibility.
scientific_record.Evidence or vv preconditions: Completion/coverage/sign-off is not adequate evidence without a bounded claim, configuration and context.
scientific_record.Expected payoff asserted at this source: The universal practice named by this row has no established general payoff. Any plausible benefit belongs to its bounded alternative in CURRENT_ASSESSMENT and MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM; compare that alternative with its costs and cheaper paths. Do not attribute the replacement mechanism's intended benefit to the rejected universal.
scientific_record.Decision or consumer: No legitimate universal consumer; retain only context-specific users of the underlying stronger property.
scientific_record.Known failure modes: Bureaucratic accumulation, gaming, false confidence, delayed feedback and tool/process lock-in.
scientific_record.Important criticisms: Modern 15288 is lifecycle-model neutral; historical V lineages were plural and the Forsberg–Mooz Vee addressed concurrent engineering.
scientific_record.How the property evolved: Original form: Complete decomposition/specification once, then implement, integrate and validate once in a fixed sequence. Evolved under criticism into: Iterative, concurrent and recursive SE with context-specific staging and controlled baselines.
scientific_record.Evolved form in this source: Iterative, concurrent and recursive SE with context-specific staging and controlled baselines.
scientific_record.Ceremony vs property: The candidate is itself a ceremony, caricature or overclaim. Any useful residue is represented by another admitted property.
scientific_record.Empirical or domain evidence: Strong historical and current-standard evidence against universal retention.
scientific_record.Contrary evidence: Some high-consequence physical programmes need staged maturity and irreversible transitions, but not a universal one-pass model.
scientific_record.Open questions: Which physical/certification constraints justify particular gates without generalising them?

Interface assumption profile.Property: Standards or process compliance as proof of system coherence or ROI
Interface assumption profile.Interface scope: Physical, logical, data, timing, state/mode, protocol, organisational, authority and environmental dimensions as applicable.
Interface assumption profile.Owner: Both endpoints plus joint resolution/escalation authority; a document custodian alone is insufficient.
Interface assumption profile.Semantics: Units, ranges, meaning, timing, failure/degraded behaviour and provenance are explicit at risk-appropriate precision.
Interface assumption profile.Assumptions: Cross-boundary assumptions are owned, current and testable/monitorable.
Interface assumption profile.Version identity: Endpoint, contract, tool/data and environment versions are bound to evidence.
Interface assumption profile.Change notification: Change impact, compatibility window and revalidation responsibilities are explicit.
Interface assumption profile.Verification: Check each side's conformance to the contract.
Interface assumption profile.Integration: Exercise composition and end-to-end interactions in a credible context.
Interface assumption profile.Degradation: Fallback, error handling and residual incompatibility are represented where consequential.
Interface assumption profile.Cheap path: Outside such obligations, adopt only provisions with real decision/failure consumers.
Interface assumption profile.Mature form: Evidence-bound use of standards: compliance is a constraint or coordination mechanism, not a general certificate of coherence, fitness or ROI; a defined compliance outcome can still be legitimately certified.

Configuration change profile.Property: Standards or process compliance as proof of system coherence or ROI
Configuration change profile.Identified items: All representations/products/environments whose identity can change the claim or decision.
Configuration change profile.Baseline or current state: Authoritative current composition and supersession are explicit; a baseline is not presumed frozen forever.
Configuration change profile.Change authority: Approval does not manufacture technical truth.
Configuration change profile.Impact scope: Requirements, architecture, assumptions, interfaces, suppliers, models, code/hardware, tests, operations and claims as material.
Configuration change profile.Status accounting: Decision, implementation, rollout, exception and actual operational state are distinguished.
Configuration change profile.Evidence currentness: Evidence cites configuration and has invalidation/reuse rules.
Configuration change profile.Rollback or recovery: Required where change consequence and reversibility justify it.
Configuration change profile.Cheap path: Outside such obligations, adopt only provisions with real decision/failure consumers.
Configuration change profile.Mature form: Evidence-bound use of standards: compliance is a constraint or coordination mechanism, not a general certificate of coherence, fitness or ROI; a defined compliance outcome can still be legitimately certified.

Integration profile.Property: Standards or process compliance as proof of system coherence or ROI
Integration profile.Integration objective: Expose the highest-value composition uncertainty early enough to change design/action.
Integration profile.Sequence: Risk-, dependency- and learning-ordered rather than merely schedule-ordered.
Integration profile.Entry identity: Exact component/model/software/data/environment versions and readiness evidence.
Integration profile.Environment or surrogate: Fidelity, intended use, omissions and correlation are explicit.
Integration profile.Interface targets: Semantic, timing, state, physical, organisational and failure interactions.
Integration profile.Anomaly flow: Observation, configuration, hypothesis, disposition, waiver and regression remain linked.
Integration profile.Regression: Selected from change impact and prior failure mechanisms.
Integration profile.Cheap path: Outside such obligations, adopt only provisions with real decision/failure consumers.
Integration profile.Mature form: Evidence-bound use of standards: compliance is a constraint or coordination mechanism, not a general certificate of coherence, fitness or ROI; a defined compliance outcome can still be legitimately certified.

Verification validation profile.Property: Standards or process compliance as proof of system coherence or ROI
Verification validation profile.Claim: A specific requirement, architecture/interface proposition, model-use claim, mission/use claim or change-equivalence claim.
Verification validation profile.Verification question: Does the identified configuration satisfy the specified claim?
Verification validation profile.Validation question: Does it fulfil the current intended use/need in the relevant context?
Verification validation profile.Method: Test, analysis, inspection, demonstration, simulation, operational evidence or combination selected for discrimination and cost.
Verification validation profile.Environment and data: Representative enough for the claim; provenance, fidelity and limitations explicit.
Verification validation profile.Independence: Proportionate to consequence, producer incentives and claim uncertainty.
Verification validation profile.Coverage and limits: Coverage is stated but never equated with absence of unknown behaviour.
Verification validation profile.Anomalies: Contradictory and unresolved evidence remains visible.
Verification validation profile.Currentness: Bound to configuration, assumptions, intended use and change impact.
Verification validation profile.Cheap path: Outside such obligations, adopt only provisions with real decision/failure consumers.
Verification validation profile.Mature form: Evidence-bound use of standards: compliance is a constraint or coordination mechanism, not a general certificate of coherence, fitness or ROI; a defined compliance outcome can still be legitimately certified.

Model or digital profile.Property: Standards or process compliance as proof of system coherence or ROI
Model or digital profile.Model or data purpose: Named question, decision or evidence use; no value claim from existence or volume.
Model or digital profile.Authoritative scope: Authority is claim- and use-specific, never automatic truth.
Model or digital profile.Intended use and limits: Permissible decisions, assumptions, uncertainty, fidelity and caveats.
Model or digital profile.Provenance: Model/metamodel/tool/version, data and transformations are identified.
Model or digital profile.Parity: Implementation/physical/test/environment relations and permitted divergence are explicit.
Model or digital profile.Interoperability: Semantic mapping and transformation losses are tested; open export/API and exit path considered.
Model or digital profile.Validation: Credibility evidence proportionate to decision consequence.
Model or digital profile.Currentness: Refresh latency, event triggers and stale-state signalling are explicit.
Model or digital profile.Cheap path: Outside such obligations, adopt only provisions with real decision/failure consumers.

Stakeholder or mission profile.Property: Standards or process compliance as proof of system coherence or ROI
Stakeholder or mission profile.Mission or need: No artefact or process count can substitute for authoritative stakeholder/mission grounding.
Stakeholder or mission profile.Stakeholders and lifecycle standing: Identify requesters, users, operators, maintainers, acquirers, regulators, support/disposal actors and affected external parties only where they change the governing claim or consequence.
Stakeholder or mission profile.Authority: Approval does not manufacture technical truth.
Stakeholder or mission profile.Intended use and context: State the intended use, operational conditions, external actors and validity interval relevant to this property; no generic stakeholder list substitutes.
Stakeholder or mission profile.Constraints and assumptions: Distinguish authorised constraints from preferences and proposed solutions; own and expire material assumptions.
Stakeholder or mission profile.Currentness: Re-establish after mission, authority, use-context, interface or configuration change.
Stakeholder or mission profile.Validation: Confirm that the governing stakeholder/mission claim remains legitimate and current enough for the decision.
Stakeholder or mission profile.Cheap path: Outside such obligations, adopt only provisions with real decision/failure consumers.
Stakeholder or mission profile.Mature form: Evidence-bound use of standards: compliance is a constraint or coordination mechanism, not a general certificate of coherence, fitness or ROI; a defined compliance outcome can still be legitimately certified.

Current assessment.Selected proposition: Reject process or standards compliance as sufficient proof of system coherence or general return on investment.
Current assessment.Guard and unproved premises: Compliance can impose legitimate constraints and aid coordination; causal outcomes depend on actual design, interactions, use and wider incentives.
Current assessment.Consumer: Interpreting compliance and investment claims
Current assessment.Cost adverse and cheap nontrigger: Meet applicable obligations proportionately; do not discard useful standards because they cannot guarantee success.
Current assessment.Residual uncertainty: Effect magnitude, maintenance economics and transport to a new domain are not established by the native status or this mechanism assessment. Additional local evidence may change the decision.
Current assessment.Native preservation: All original claim fields and eight technical profiles remain attached. Supporting/inapplicable profile markers retain their meaning; they are not mandatory controls.
